recognize_zh: 鐵染色（Prussian blue）配紅色核複染下，數顆紅血球母細胞的核周圍出現藍綠色鐵顆粒，部分沿核周排列成環狀或半環狀，符合環狀鐵粒母細胞（ringed sideroblasts）。
features: Erythroid precursors with blue-green siderotic granules arranged around the nucleus
Several granules encircle a substantial portion of the nuclear circumference (ring or partial ring)
Other erythroblasts contain only a few scattered granules
Nuclei stained red (nuclear fast red/safranin counterstain); cellular marrow with mixed precursors
No large iron aggregates in this field to assess storage iron
describe_en: Iron-stained bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular field of mixed precursors. Several erythroblasts contain coarse blue siderotic granules distributed perinuclearly, some forming rings or partial rings around the nucleus, while others show only scattered granules. A formal count of ringed sideroblasts (at least 5 granules covering at least one third of the nuclear circumference) as a percentage of erythroblasts is required. Findings are consistent with ringed sideroblasts; in a reactive setting, consider alcohol, copper deficiency, zinc toxicity or drugs such as isoniazid before a clonal sideroblastic process.

ddx.vs: Normal sideroblasts have one to a few small granules randomly scattered in the cytoplasm rather than a perinuclear ring.
Morphology alone cannot separate clonal from reactive causes; dysplasia, cytogenetics and SF3B1 mutation testing are needed.
Congenital forms present in young patients with microcytosis and family history, whereas acquired forms are often normo/macrocytic; genetic testing confirms.
